title: Move It, Mutate It, Block It

scenes.tts: How did anyone find a nuclear address, or prove what it does? Chapter one showed receptors reading labels, with Ran controlling where cargo loads and unloads.
scenes.visual: Open on chapter 1's carried cutaway, filling the frame: cytoplasm left, nucleus right, double grey nuclear membrane, one large central pore with waving teal FG chains. A yellow cargo with a blue NLS tab is already centre-frame; a bright magnifying-glass outline settles over the tab with a question mark beside it. Behind that question, a blue importin complex moves inward and a purple CRM1 complex with orange-tagged cargo and green RanGTP moves outward. Green RanGTP tokens fill the nucleus and grey RanGDP tokens the cytoplasm. Keep SCHEMATIC at top right.
scenes.narration: How did anyone find a nuclear address, or prove what it does? Chapter one showed receptors reading labels, with Ran controlling where cargo loads and unloads.

scenes.visual: Dim the moving cutaway and overlay the title MOVE IT, MUTATE IT, BLOCK IT for 1.5 seconds; lift it without changing the layout.

scenes.tts: Start with nucleoplasmin, a frog oocyte protein of five copies, each with a tail. In nineteen eighty-two, Dingwall, Sharnick and Laskey clipped the tails away. Bare cores injected into the cytoplasm stayed out. A larger pentamer keeping one tail went in.
scenes.caption: Start with nucleoplasmin, a frog oocyte protein of five copies, each with a tail. In 1982, Dingwall, Sharnick and Laskey clipped the tails away. Bare cores injected into the cytoplasm stayed out. A larger pentamer keeping one tail went in.
scenes.visual: Same cutaway, labelled FROG OOCYTE (schematic). A yellow pentagon core with five short blue tails appears in the cytoplasm; small grey scissors snip the tails off one by one. A grey needle injects bare cores into the cytoplasm: they drift to the pore, bump the teal chains and stay left. A second needle injects a core that kept one blue tail, visibly larger than the bare core; it threads slowly through the pore and arrives in the nucleus. Labels: NO TAILS: OUT and ONE TAIL: IN.
scenes.narration: Start with nucleoplasmin, a frog oocyte protein of five copies, each with a tail. In 1982, Dingwall, Sharnick and Laskey clipped the tails away. Bare cores injected into the cytoplasm stayed out. A larger pentamer keeping one tail went in.

scenes.tts: One attached tail was sufficient for final accumulation. More tails changed the rate, not how much eventually reached the nucleus.
scenes.visual: Keep the same cutaway. Beside the one-tail pentamer, add a matching pentamer with five blue tails. Both finish in the nucleus, but the five-tail pentamer moves faster. Labels: ONE TAIL: SUFFICIENT and MORE TAILS: FASTER. Keep SCHEMATIC visible.
scenes.narration: One attached tail was sufficient for final accumulation. More tails changed the rate, not how much eventually reached the nucleus.

scenes.tts: One more injection put bare cores straight into the nucleus. They remained there. Why that injection matters is a question the page asks you.
scenes.visual: A third grey needle enters the nucleus from the right edge and leaves bare yellow cores there; they drift gently on the nuclear side. A dashed outline circles this third needle with a small question mark. Show nothing that states a conclusion; the two earlier results stay visible on the left, faded to half brightness.
scenes.narration: One more injection put bare cores straight into the nucleus. They remained there. Why that injection matters is a question the page asks you.

scenes.tts: Which route does cargo take? In nineteen eighty-four, Feldherr and colleagues injected gold grains coated with nucleoplasmin. The coated grains spanned about five to twenty nanometres. They entered the nucleus. Electron microscopy located transport at the pores.
scenes.caption: Which route does cargo take? In 1984, Feldherr and colleagues injected gold grains coated with nucleoplasmin. The coated grains spanned about 5 to 20 nm. They entered the nucleus. Electron microscopy located transport at the pores.
scenes.visual: Shift the cutaway to a grainy black-and-white electron-micrograph look, labelled schematic, keeping the same layout. Small gold dots, each with a yellow halo coat, are injected on the left. Some enter the nucleus. Of the grains caught interacting with the envelope, show them only at pore openings, with several in pore profiles. A small label reads TRANSPORT AT PORES.
scenes.narration: Which route does cargo take? In 1984, Feldherr and colleagues injected gold grains coated with nucleoplasmin. The coated grains spanned about 5 to 20 nm. They entered the nucleus. Electron microscopy located transport at the pores.

scenes.tts: Now predict. Coat the same gold with an inert polymer instead of nucleoplasmin. Where will most of the grains end up?
scenes.visual: Swap in fresh gold dots with dull grey halos labelled INERT COAT, injected on the left. Across the top, the question WHERE DO THEY END UP? The micrograph texture and teal chains keep moving slowly.
scenes.narration: Now predict. Coat the same gold with an inert polymer instead of nucleoplasmin. Where will most of the grains end up?

scenes.visual: Hold for 4.5 seconds: the grey-coated gold drifts in the cytoplasm near the membrane, FG chains wave, the question stays on screen. Reveal nothing.

scenes.tts: Mostly outside the nucleus. Gold coated with nucleoplasmin lacking its transport part was also largely kept out. So the coat, not the gold, decided entry.
scenes.visual: The grey-coated grains stay mostly on the cytoplasmic side. A third batch, gold with a yellow coat missing its blue tail region, also stays mostly outside. Beside them the yellow-coated grains with full coats sit at and through the pore. A label settles: THE COAT DECIDES.
scenes.narration: Mostly outside the nucleus. Gold coated with nucleoplasmin lacking its transport part was also largely kept out. So the coat, not the gold, decided entry.

scenes.tts: Next, a label you could move. Kalderon, Smith and colleagues traced the address of S V forty large T antigen to a short stretch. The normally cytoplasmic reporters were beta galactosidase and pyruvate kinase. Attached to either one, the stretch caused nuclear accumulation.
scenes.caption: Next, a label you could move. Kalderon, Smith and colleagues traced the address of SV40 large T antigen to a short stretch. The normally cytoplasmic reporters were β-galactosidase and pyruvate kinase. Attached to either one, the stretch caused nuclear accumulation.
scenes.visual: Return to the colour cutaway. A yellow block labelled SV40 LARGE T carries a short blue tab, PKKKRKV in large letters. The tab lifts off and clips onto two large pale blocks on the left labelled REPORTER 1 and REPORTER 2 (cytoplasmic). Both reporters, now tagged, thread the pore and gather in the nucleus while untagged copies stay left.
scenes.narration: Next, a label you could move. Kalderon, Smith and colleagues traced the address of SV40 large T antigen to a short stretch. The normally cytoplasmic reporters were β-galactosidase and pyruvate kinase. Attached to either one, the stretch caused nuclear accumulation.

scenes.tts: Next, change it. Swapping lysine one hundred twenty-eight for threonine abolished nuclear accumulation. Moving, mutating, and blocking are complementary tests. Each result supports only a limited claim.
scenes.caption: Next, change it. Swapping lysine 128 for threonine abolished nuclear accumulation. Moving, mutating, and blocking are complementary tests. Each result supports only a limited claim.
scenes.visual: Zoom on the blue tab: one K letter flips to T and the tab turns grey. The T antigen block with the grey tab stays on the cytoplasmic side. Then three icons line up across the top, built from the scenes so far: an arrow (MOVE), a swapped letter (MUTATE), and an empty red stop sign (BLOCK) that has not been used yet.
scenes.narration: Next, change it. Swapping lysine 128 for threonine abolished nuclear accumulation. Moving, mutating, and blocking are complementary tests. Each result supports only a limited claim.

scenes.tts: By nineteen ninety-five, importin alpha was shown to recognize the signal. Importin beta was shown to dock at the pore. Leucine-rich export signals still had no known reader.
scenes.caption: By 1995, importin α was shown to recognize the signal. Importin β was shown to dock at the pore. Leucine-rich export signals still had no known reader.
scenes.visual: The blue importin alpha shape closes around the blue tab; importin beta joins and touches the teal FG chains, exactly as in chapter 1. On the nuclear side, a yellow cargo with an orange tab labelled LEUCINE-RICH NES waits alone, with a question mark where a reader should be.
scenes.narration: By 1995, importin α was shown to recognize the signal. Importin β was shown to dock at the pore. Leucine-rich export signals still had no known reader.

scenes.tts: In nineteen ninety-seven, Fornerod, Mattaj and colleagues tested C R M one. Extra C R M one stimulated export of Rev. It also stimulated export of U s n R N As. Leptomycin B inhibited both export pathways.
scenes.caption: In 1997, Fornerod, Mattaj and colleagues tested CRM1. Extra CRM1 stimulated export of Rev. It also stimulated export of U snRNAs. Leptomycin B inhibited both export pathways.
scenes.visual: Two panels slide in along the bottom while the cutaway keeps moving. Panel 1, MORE CRM1: extra purple crescents appear and more orange-tagged Rev cargo and U snRNA cargo move out. Panel 2, LEPTOMYCIN B: a red LMB stop symbol overlays CRM1 without implying a molecular binding site, and both cargoes remain nuclear. The BLOCK stop sign at the top turns solid red.
scenes.narration: In 1997, Fornerod, Mattaj and colleagues tested CRM1. Extra CRM1 stimulated export of Rev. It also stimulated export of U snRNAs. Leptomycin B inhibited both export pathways.

scenes.tts: C R M one, Ran G T P, and an export signal formed a complex in vitro. All three results pointed at C R M one. Together, they made a stronger case than any one result alone.
scenes.caption: CRM1, RanGTP and an export signal formed a complex in vitro. All three results pointed at CRM1. Together, they made a stronger case than any one result alone.
scenes.visual: Replace the two panels with one panel labelled TEST TUBE. A purple CRM1 crescent, orange-tagged cargo and green RanGTP token assemble together; keep the shapes schematic and do not show atomic contacts. Then three arrows rise from icons for extra CRM1, LMB and the assembled complex. They converge on a single purple CRM1 crescent, which brightens as the panels fade into the cutaway.
scenes.narration: CRM1, RanGTP and an export signal formed a complex in vitro. All three results pointed at CRM1. Together, they made a stronger case than any one result alone.

scenes.tts: The same year, Izaurralde, Görlich and colleagues collapsed the Ran gradient in oocyte nuclei. They injected Ran G A P one, Ran B P one, or a defective Ran mutant. The mutant could not stably hold G T P.
scenes.caption: The same year, Izaurralde, Görlich and colleagues collapsed the Ran gradient in oocyte nuclei. They injected RanGAP1, RanBP1, or a defective Ran mutant. The mutant could not stably hold GTP.
scenes.visual: Grey needles separately inject small teal RanGAP1 and RanBP1 shapes, or a cracked token labelled MUTANT RAN, into the nucleus. In each case, nuclear green RanGTP tokens disappear, collapsing the difference across the envelope. Label: GRADIENT COLLAPSED.
scenes.narration: The same year, Izaurralde, Görlich and colleagues collapsed the Ran gradient in oocyte nuclei. They injected RanGAP1, RanBP1, or a defective Ran mutant. The mutant could not stably hold GTP.

scenes.tts: All three treatments depleted nuclear Ran G T P. Major import and export pathways stopped. Export was more readily inhibited than import.
scenes.caption: All three treatments depleted nuclear RanGTP. Major import and export pathways stopped. Export was more readily inhibited than import.
scenes.visual: Keep the collapsed-gradient cutaway. Purple export complexes stall more readily as RanGTP is depleted; major blue import pathways also stall. Compare sensitivity without showing export stopping earlier in time. Label: EXPORT MORE SENSITIVE.
scenes.narration: All three treatments depleted nuclear RanGTP. Major import and export pathways stopped. Export was more readily inhibited than import.

scenes.tts: None of these results proved everything. Move it, mutate it, block its reader: each supports one claim. The page's drug puzzle stays unresolved.
scenes.visual: Restore the gradient: green tokens refill the nucleus and traffic resumes both ways. The three top icons MOVE, MUTATE, BLOCK glow in turn. Finally a yellow cargo with a question mark sits in the cytoplasm beside a red LMB plug, unresolved, labelled DRUG PUZZLE.
scenes.narration: None of these results proved everything. Move it, mutate it, block its reader: each supports one claim. The page's drug puzzle stays unresolved.

scenes.visual: End card over the still-moving cutaway. Large line: MOVE IT, MUTATE IT, BLOCK ITS READER: EACH SUPPORTS ONE CLAIM. Hold 3.5 seconds with slow FG-chain and Ran-token motion.
